Ana: heads up — we saw a small but recurring mismatch between the policy simulator and prod routing decisions this morning. not a full outage but a customer saw a cold-GPU fallback that sim didn't predict.
Mike: can you paste the trace? which rule fired in prod vs sim?
Ana: trace attached (trimmed). looks like cost-bucket aggregation + soft-constraint tiebreaker produced a slightly higher penalty in prod. sim uses approximate bucket sums for perf; prod uses on-the-wire counters.
Jules: hmm, we've noticed drift when using `bucketize(sum(costs), 5)` vs `sum(bucketize(costs, 5))`. order matters with rounding.
Lee: that's the classic quantization non-associativity. we should add an invariant checker in both places rather than trying to make them identical.
Ana: proposal: introduce "policy invariant watchers" that run lightweight assertions at runtime and in the sim sandbox. they would sample requests (1%) and verify a small set of invariants, emitting a structured explain_event when violation occurs.
Mike: concrete example invariant?
Ana: e.g. `total_penalty(route) <= route.max_allowed_penalty` and `preferred_region_score - fallback_score >= preference_threshold` — if they break, we emit `policy_explain: { reason: "invariant-penalty-exceeded", route, evaluated_scores }`.
Jules: love that. two implementation concerns: 1) perf overhead, 2) explosion of unique explain payloads in telemetry.
Lee: perf: keep assertions boolean, sampled, and evaluated after most cheap ops (no blocking KV lookups). Telemetry: canonicalize the explain payload into a small tag + a few numeric buckets. store a hash for deeper debug traces.
policy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 3488881800 to `canary-rtg-1` (50 req/s).
Mike: rollout plan: enable invariant watchers in sim + dev canaries first, keep sampling at 0.5% then 1% after 24h. if we hit >5 violations/hour, auto-rollback.
Ana: question: should invariants be expressible in the policy DSL or be hard-coded in runtime?
Jules: pros/cons: DSL gives product flexibility, but increases risk (users can author bogus invariants). hard-coded gives stability and easier auditing.
Lee: compromise: two layers — a curated set of runtime invariants (hard-coded) and an opt-in DSL sanity-check layer that runs only in sim and can be sandboxed.
Mike: also add a feature flag for debug explains so we don't leak internal route metadata to tenants by accident.
Ana: agree. telemetry schema: `(invariant_tag, sample_id, canonical_reason, small_numeric_vector)` — keep all fields small strings/ints. full dump only on manually triggered debug pull.
Jules: tests: sim harness should fuzz-ordering of bucket ops to catch quantization drift. add nightly job to compare sim/predictions against prod-sampled explains.
Lee: operational: metric `policy.invariant_violation{tag=..}` and alert if rate > baseline * 3. Also a burn-in period to establish baseline.
Mike: action items: 1) Ana to draft RFC for invariant watcher runtime + DSL sandbox (due EOD Tue). 2) Jules to add fuzz tests to sim harness (PR by Fri). 3) Lee to add telemetry schema & metric (PR by Thu). 4) I'll wire the canary flag and rollback hook.
Ana: thanks — I'll also include a short runbook snippet for debugging explain events.
Jules: +1 — and let's plan a 30m check-in after first canary window. :calendar:
Lee: noted.
policy-bot: reminder: please ack the canary PR at 3488880300 if you haven't.
Mike: acked.
Ana: closing the loop — I'll post the RFC link in this thread once ready.
